title: I tried to create Karambit Fade for my own CS that I made with AI. How much would you pay for this knife?
author: Minecat0

comments.author: Xay_DE
comments.body:
you couldnt get me to play this even if u gave me money, let alone buy a "skin" in that.  
there is no depth, no artistic stuff. this is quite literally a empty husk.   
and it doesnt help that no human has really put effort into this

replies.author: Minecat0
replies.body: Yes you are correct, I made this game in 10 minutes with Claude. Would you play it if I spent whole day working on it?

replies.author: Xay_DE
replies.body:
even then no, games are not something u make in a day.  
and even if u spent 10 years with claude i wouldnt pay for it.  
download godot, read its docs, watch basic tutorials and learn what u do instead of not even knowing what anything in ur game does.

replies.author: EZ_LIFE_EZ_CUCUMBER
replies.body: Vibecoding aside ... I recall when claude used to struggle solving quadratic .. interesting to see it go ahead .... did you do it all in one go or was it more step-by step workflow?

replies.author: Minecat0
replies.body: Yeah it's crazy how fast Claude has evolved... This was actually part of video where I created Counter Strike with Deepseek and Claude. The Claude part starts at 1:13 [https://youtu.be/9oobLIhRgcI?si=yPu\_Jz-0AYtDPpYb&t=73](https://youtu.be/9oobLIhRgcI?si=yPu_Jz-0AYtDPpYb&t=73)

replies.author: intLeon
replies.body: Dont mind the anti mumble. Im a senior dev and If it gets you interested take a look at what it does in the background and try to understand it. But it shouldnt push you away from having fun. Enjoy it either way.

replies.author: Minecat0
replies.body: Wow that's cool! How long did it take you to create the game and with what tools?

replies.author: Resident-Aspect4084
replies.body:
So I went out for pizza with my cousin, pulled out my laptop, and showed him my latest project - Baron Arena also in browser. 

Then he asked if we could make something similar, and within two hours, while eating pizza in the park, we had a working prototype.

We used Gemini 2.5 Pro and plain Vanilla JS.

When I got back home, I spent a few more days on it and released Blood Mood in both multiplayer and single-player modes.

Since then, I’ve been creating several other games.

Once, my 10-year-old nephew and I sat down together and made Tank War — this time, a game about tanks.

Right now, I’m working on another one about cars, written in Swift.

If you’d like, I can share links to those games.
